title: Flatness of strict-local refinement over a strict-local base
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings (the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $A$ is the maximal ideal of $R$). Choose separable closures $k_R^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and $k_A^{\mathrm{sep}}$ of their residue fields, and an embedding $k_R^{\mathrm{sep}}\to k_A^{\mathrm{sep}}$ extending the residue-field map. Let $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the strict henselizations for these choices [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Give $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ the canonical local $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-algebra structure extending $R\to A$ and the chosen residue embedding. Then the multiplication homomorphism
$$A\otimes_R R^{\mathrm{sh}}\longrightarrow A^{\mathrm{sh}},\qquad a\otimes r\longmapsto a r,$$
is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Here tensor products and their scalar actions are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-module-base-change]. There is no Noetherian or finite-type assumption on $R\to A$.

source.place: Tag 08HV (lemma-strictly-henselian-functorial-improve), flatness consequence: the canonical refinement is a localization followed by strict henselization.

proof.text: By [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization, lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples], both $R\to R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $A\to A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ are filtered colimits of etale algebras of finite presentation, hence are ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. The pointed-algebra and triple presentations agree: a point $\chi:E\to K$ gives the prime $\ker\chi$ and its residue-field embedding into $K$, and a triple gives their composite $E\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to K$; these inverse constructions preserve morphisms. Apply the triples statement at the maximal ideals, with the separable closures specified in the item.

source.place: Tag 04GW (lemma-strict-henselization-different), statement and pointed-algebra description in the proof; Tag 08HV, proof through lemma-henselian-functorial-improve.

proof.text: Set $T=A\otimes_R R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ with its left $A$-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-module-base-change]. Base-change stability in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], applied to $R\to R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ along $R\to A$, makes $A\to T$ ind-etale. No flatness of $R\to A$ is needed for this base change.

source.place: Tag 08HV (lemma-strictly-henselian-functorial-improve), proof via lemma-henselian-functorial-improve: filtered-colimit argument using Tag 04GW (lemma-strict-henselization-different) and Tag 08HS (lemma-colimits-of-etale).

proof.text: Let $h:R^{\mathrm{sh}}\to A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the canonical local map fixed in the statement, and $i:A\to A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ its structural map. Since $h$ and $i$ agree on $R$, $(a,r)\mapsto i(a)h(r)$ is $R$-balanced and bilinear, so [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $\psi:T\to A^{\mathrm{sh}}$. The identities $\psi((a\otimes r)(b\otimes s))=i(ab)h(rs)=\psi(a\otimes r)\psi(b\otimes s)$ and $\psi(1\otimes1)=1$ show it is a ring map, since pure tensors generate $T$ additively. Also $\psi(a\otimes1)=i(a)$, so it is an $A$-algebra map. Both $T$ and $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ are ind-etale over $A$ by steps 1 and 2. Apply the relative clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] with base $A$, source $T$ and target $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$: $\psi$ is ind-etale and therefore weakly etale. This is exactly the specified multiplication map.

source.place: Tag 08HV (lemma-strictly-henselian-functorial-improve), proof via lemma-henselian-functorial-improve: filtered-colimit argument using Tag 04GW (lemma-strict-henselization-different) and Tag 08HS (lemma-colimits-of-etale).

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], weak etaleness of $\psi$ includes that $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is flat as a $T$-module via $\psi$. This is flatness of the ring map $\psi$ by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], proving the assertion.

reviewed_lean.note: Only the lean record changes; the statement field is verbatim in the file; proof is sorry; docstrings carry the source/blueprint and all 4 proof steps. Clauses match the node: local R→A via IsLocalHom; separable residue closures KR, KA with scalar towers; ι extends ResidueField.map (_hι); R^sh, A^sh via the recorded StrictHenselizationPresentationIn; canonical h given by its 04GU characterization (R-algebra map, IsLocalHom, residue equation), which exists and is unique, so the statement is not weakened. Conclusion: (AlgHom.liftEquiv R A H C h).toRingHom.Flat, the a⊗r↦a·h(r) map; flatness only, not faithful flatness. No Noetherian, finite-type or flat assumption; independent universes u, v, max u w, max v z. Edge cases fine: identity, k[ε]→k, ℚ→ℚ(i), inseparable residue extensions. No duplicate in Sheaf/WeilConjectures/Mathlib. Advisory: IsLocalRing H/C are instance hypotheses, harmless because strict henselizations are local.
